strengths: Novel mathematical framework formally defining LLM DNA via bi-Lipschitz maps with sound theoretical proofs (Lemma 3.2, Theorems 3.4-3.5, 4.1), elegantly connecting functional distance to inheritance and genetic determinism properties

Practical training-free extraction pipeline that is scalable and extensible to new models without recomputation, addressing key limitations of EmbedLLM and supporting both open and closed-source models

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 305 LLMs from 153 organizations with multiple evaluation angles (relationship detection, model routing, phylogenetic analysis) and robustness validation via Mantel test showing stability across different datasets (Pearson r > 0.75)

Interesting practical insights including undocumented model relationships and phylogenetic tree alignment with known architectural shifts and temporal progression, providing value for LLM governance and ecosystem understanding
Rigorous theoretical analysis with concentration bounds (Lemma 5.2) for empirical approximation and constructive existence proof directly yielding a practical algorithm
weaknesses: Substantial gap between theory and practice: theory assumes bounded input space with probability measure μ and outputs as logits, while practice uses 600 deterministic prompts and semantic embeddings; no empirical validation that theoretical bi-Lipschitz constants (c1, c2) are tight or meaningful

Hard dependency on specific embedding model (Qwen3-Embedding-8B) not adequately discussed, contradicting 'LLM-agnostic' claims; no ablation studies showing robustness to embedding model choice or whether different embeddings produce conflicting DNAs
Marginal practical improvements on concrete tasks (model routing: 0.672 vs 0.665 for EmbedLLM, ~1% difference with 11 missing models complicating comparison) undermine claims of practical utility

Relationship detection evaluation uses incomplete Hugging Face ground truth; higher recall than precision (0.916 vs 0.858) could indicate either undocumented relationships or method permissiveness; weak baselines and no comparison to Zhu et al. (2025)

Phylogenetic tree lacks quantitative validation; alignment with architecture/temporal progression is observed but unquantified; no comparison to alternative tree construction or analysis of whether structure arises from parameter counts/release dates rather than functional behavior

Missing ablation studies on critical design choices: DNA dimension (L=128), sample size (t=600), embedding concatenation strategy, random projection type; no sensitivity analysis for any hyperparameters
Limited scope: 100M-70B parameter range only, text generation models only, no study of how results generalize to different model scales or modalities; claims of 'general' approach not fully justified

Large-scale evaluation across 305 LLMs with comprehensive experimental scope
Training-free and computationally efficient extraction pipeline applicable to closed-source models
Stability demonstrated via Mantel test showing consistent DNA distances across different datasets (Pearson-R=0.7797)

weaknesses: Critical theory-practice gap: theoretical framework assumes finite Sm space but practical pipeline uses 600 samples; no empirical verification that extracted DNA satisfies claimed bi-Lipschitz properties or that random projection preserves them in practice

Arbitrary theoretical definition: why bi-Lipschitz mapping represents 'DNA' is unjustified; biological analogy is misleading since DNA causally specifies phenotype while this is merely distance-preserving compression; no analysis of actual bi-Lipschitz constants c1, c2

Embedding model choice inadequately explored: entire method depends on Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B as universal encoder but no ablation studies on choice of embedding model, contrary to LLM-agnosticism claim
Limited practical novelty: extraction pipeline (embed→concatenate→random project) is straightforward application of established dimensionality reduction

Questionable validation: relationship detection validated against incomplete Hugging Face ground truth, then mismatches attributed to 'undocumented relationships' (circular reasoning); case studies are anecdotal without independent verification
Weak practical improvements: model routing shows marginal 0.672 vs 0.665 improvement over EmbedLLM (statistically insignificant, not apples-to-apples comparison)

Missing critical ablations: no justification for L=128 dimension choice, no sensitivity analysis to number of samples (600), no comparison to simpler baselines (averaging, PCA), no analysis of dataset-specificity of DNA

Phylogenetic tree validation is qualitative: clustering by functional similarity naturally groups same-family models; claims about different evolutionary speeds lack quantitative validation or independent verification

Incomplete theoretical analysis: no computation of actual bi-Lipschitz constants, dimension bound L=O(ϵ^-2 log K) never calculated for actual 305 models, assumes deterministic LLM outputs conflicting with stochasticity in practice
Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned, specific embedding model version critical but not fully specified, some hyperparameter choices (temperature=0.7) lack justification

strengths: Novel and principled theoretical framework: Formalizes LLM DNA as a bi-Lipschitz representation, addressing key limitations of prior task-specific or relative approaches. Definition 3.3 is elegant and well-motivated.

Rigorous mathematical foundations: Solid proofs establishing Hilbert space structure (Lemma 3.2), inheritance/genetic determinism properties (Theorems 3.4-3.5), and existence via Johnson-Lindenstrauss (Theorem 4.1). All proofs appear correct.

Scalable training-free algorithm: Algorithm 1 using random Gaussian projection is simple, computationally efficient, and works with closed-source APIs without retraining when new models are added—a key advantage over EmbedLLM.

Large-scale comprehensive evaluation: Experiments span 305 models across 153 organizations and multiple perspectives (relationship detection, model routing, stability analysis, phylogenetic trees), providing substantial evidence of applicability.

Strong stability results: Mantel test (Figure 3) demonstrates that DNA structure is robust across disjoint dataset combinations (Pearson-r=0.78, p<0.001), validating the intrinsic nature of the representation.

Interesting empirical findings: Undocumented model relationships (Table 4, Figure 4), fine-tuned models clustering near base models, and evolutionary tree alignment with architectural/temporal shifts provide actionable insights.
Well-presented and reproducible: Clear motivation from biological DNA analogy, logical flow from theory to practice, comprehensive appendices with full model list, proofs, and experimental details.
weaknesses: Theory-practice gap under-explored: Theory assumes finite input space and exact Hilbert distance computation; practice uses stochastic approximation with finite samples (Definition 5.1). While Lemma 5.2 provides concentration bounds, the paper lacks empirical analysis of how sample size t=600 affects DNA quality and doesn't discuss the variance of the approximation.

Critical design choices lack justification and ablation: (1) Embedding model (Qwen3-Embedding-8B) chosen without sensitivity analysis—different embeddings capture different semantics and could significantly affect DNA. (2) Sample size and dataset selection (600 samples from 6 specific datasets) appear arbitrary without justification. (3) DNA dimension fixed at 128 without relating to theoretical bounds L = O((c₂+c₁)/(c₂-c₁))² log K), whose constants c₁, c₂ are never estimated.

Modest practical improvements: Model routing (Table 2) shows only 0.7% improvement over EmbedLLM (0.672 vs 0.665). While DNA uses no task-specific training (a strength), the marginal gain limits demonstrated practical impact. 11 model failures in comparison data further complicate assessment.

Weak baselines for relationship detection: Section 6.2 compares against only Random and Greedy baselines. No quantitative comparison with Zhu et al. (2025) fingerprinting or other methods mentioned in related work. Figure 2 shows only qualitative agreement, making it unclear whether improvements stem from the novel definition or engineering/scale.

Undocumented relationships lack validation: Table 4 lists predictions without ground truth verification. Appendix C.2 acknowledges false positives but doesn't quantify true positive rates. Claims of 'discovering' relationships are speculative without manual verification against model cards or alternative documentation.

Limited scope of demonstrated applications: Introduction motivates safety auditing, governance, and multi-agent systems, but experiments only validate relationship detection and model routing. Significant gap between motivation and demonstrated use cases reduces practical significance.

Theory-practice gap in finite input assumption: Definition 3.1 bounds input sequences by maximum length m, making the input space finite. This is computationally intractable for practical m. While acknowledged, the implications for the validity of theoretical guarantees in practice remain unclear.

Incomplete evaluation of evolutionary tree: Phylogenetic tree alignment with known architectural/temporal shifts is somewhat expected since functional behavior likely correlates with these factors. More rigorous validation (e.g., prediction of held-out model relationships) would strengthen this claim.

strengths: Novel theoretical framework: Rigorous formal definition of LLM DNA via bi-Lipschitz maps, with elegant existence proof using Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma and formal derivations of inheritance and genetic determinism properties

Practical, scalable solution: Training-free RepTrace pipeline applicable to heterogeneous LLMs with different architectures and tokenizers; works with closed-source APIs; enables incremental updates without recomputation

Comprehensive experimental validation: Large-scale evaluation on 305 models from 153 organizations; multi-faceted assessment (relationship detection with AUC 0.992 vs PhyloLM 0.788, model routing, phylogenetic analysis); extensive stress tests on heterogeneous datasets, random inputs, chat templates, and fine-tuning intensity
High-impact application: Addresses critical problem of managing rapidly proliferating LLM ecosystem with clear use cases in license governance, model selection, and safety risk propagation
Reproducibility and transparency: Complete proofs, hyperparameters, full model list, promised code/demo release; honest discussion of limitations in dedicated section

Phylogenetic analysis shows meaningful structure: LLM DNA-based tree aligns with known architectural shifts (encoder-decoder to decoder-only), temporal progression, and distinct evolutionary speeds across families
Robustness of method: Stability across different sentence-embedding models demonstrated via Mantel tests; performance remains stable across dataset heterogeneity (r > 0.75)
weaknesses: Theory-practice gap: Definition 3.1 assumes LLM function maps to logits for all output sequences in bounded input space (unrealistic for variable-length context); Stochastic Functional Distance bridges gap ad hoc without rigorous connection to theoretical d_H; choice of concatenation over aggregation (averaging, attention) unexplained; relationship between theoretical dimension formula and practical choice L=128 unclear

Semantic embedding dependency: DNA critically depends on choice of embedding model (Qwen3, BGE, MPNet), yet claims to be 'intrinsic'; dependency not accounted for in theory; introduces potential bias from embedding model's semantic view; raises fundamental question of whether DNA is truly intrinsic or view through particular embedding lens

Unexplained robustness to random inputs: DNA actually performs *better* on random 100-word strings (AUC 0.987) than benchmark data (0.979), undermining claims about semantic significance; authors explain as capturing 'relative relationships' but this suggests DNA may capture superficial artifacts rather than learned knowledge; deserves deeper investigation

Limited baseline comparisons: Only PhyloLM as serious baseline; missing comparisons to parameter similarity, activation similarity, other tokenizer-aware metrics; EmbedLLM routing comparison compromised by removal of 11 models and different experimental setup from original

Evaluation methodological issues: Ground truth (HuggingFace Model Tree) is incomplete and acknowledged as such; makes precision/recall metrics difficult to interpret; higher recall than precision suggests labeled false positives are likely true positives; limited evaluation on downstream tasks (only routing and relationship detection, not performance prediction where PhyloLM was designed)

Scope limitations: Evaluation restricted to text-generation models (decoder-only and encoder-decoder); no multimodal, vision-language, or specialized architectures; all models from HuggingFace; no proprietary/closed models; scalability for very large K unknown (L=128 empirically chosen; C.5 acknowledges larger L may be needed for >300 models)

Technical gaps: Probability bound 1-2/K² in Corollary 3.4 not explicitly discussed for K=305; Cmax in concentration bound not characterized; choice of Euclidean distance in DNA space not justified; tightness of bi-Lipschitz constants c1, c2 unexplored; variance of DNA across different random matrix seeds not tested

Practical details missing: Computational cost of DNA extraction not reported; whether DNA can be updated incrementally vs. requires recomputation; impact of fixed random projection matrix A on stability

strengths: Clear motivation addressing the important problem of understanding relationships among millions of LLMs in the ecosystem
Formal theoretical framework with mathematically sound existence proof via Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma and well-defined bi-Lipschitz DNA properties
Large-scale empirical evaluation across 305 models with thorough ablation studies (embedding models, DNA dimension, parameter size bias, fine-tuning effects)
Training-free, scalable approach that doesn't require task-specific training, enabling application to new models without recomputation
Strong relationship detection performance (AUC 0.992 vs PhyloLM's 0.788) and competitive routing accuracy without task-specific optimization
Comprehensive reproducibility commitment with promised code release, hyperparameter details, and PyPI package
weaknesses: Substantial gap between theory and practice: theoretical framework assumes outputs are logits over all sequences with Hilbert distance, but practice uses semantic embeddings and concatenated vectors from 600 samples. No rigorous justification for why this instantiates theoretical DNA or preserves bi-Lipschitz properties.

Critical architectural choice of semantic embeddings inadequately justified: replacing theoretical output space with external Qwen3-8B embeddings is a major design decision that fundamentally changes what is measured, with insufficient analysis of lost/gained properties and potential biases in the embedding space

Evaluation methodology concerns: uses incomplete HuggingFace Model Tree as ground truth, but C.2 shows many 'false positives' are actually related models not documented, undermining ground truth reliability. Routing evaluation removed 11 failed models, risking systematic bias.

Theory-practice mismatch on functional distance: Definition 4.1 (Stochastic Functional Distance) is a statistical expectation over samples, but connection to theoretical Hilbert distance is unclear. Lemma 4.2's concentration bound is standard Hoeffding; no analysis of whether practical setting satisfies assumptions.

Limited practical novelty: core technique (semantic embeddings + random projection) is straightforward. Improvements over baselines are incremental (routing: 0.672 vs 0.665 for EmbedLLM), making it hard to justify the added theoretical machinery.

Biological DNA metaphor is overreaching: inheritance and genetic determinism follow directly from bi-Lipschitz definition; DNA subsequences lack mathematical meaning (acknowledged in limitations); phylogenetic observations are mostly confirmatory of known facts (decoder-only is recent, model families cluster together)
Claimed discoveries about undocumented relationships are weak: Table 5 mostly shows relationships within the same organization/family (Qwen3 variants), which is unsurprising and not clearly valuable

Limited model coverage despite size: heavily skewed toward 7-13B models with many variants of same base models (10+ Llama versions, 15+ Qwen versions). Missing very large models (70B+) and proprietary APIs. Limits generalizability claims.

Hyperparameter choices under-justified: DNA dimension L=128 chosen post-hoc from ablation; 600 prompts selected without justification or sensitivity analysis; Theorem 3.3's dimension formula depends on undefined bi-Lipschitz constants c1, c2

Security and robustness limitations: acknowledged as vulnerable to adaptive attacks if extraction data is known; requires closed-source extraction datasets, limiting applicability for transparency-critical use cases like license governance

Phylogenetic tree analysis is anecdotal: encoder-decoder predating decoder-only is known; 'evolutionary speeds' lack quantitative validation; t-SNE visualization can create artifacts and claims about undocumented relationships in Figure 4 are subjective

strengths: Novel theoretical framework: Formal definition of LLM DNA via bi-Lipschitz embeddings with inheritance and genetic determinism properties; elegant use of Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma for existence proof
Rigorous mathematical foundations: Theorems 3.3 and A.2-A.3 properly formulated and proved; concentration bounds (Lemma 4.2) provide statistical guarantees

Practical and scalable approach: Training-free, works without model internals or parameter access, handles diverse architectures/tokenizers, compatible with closed-source APIs, simple to implement (random Gaussian projection)

Comprehensive empirical validation: Large-scale evaluation on 305 LLMs from 153 organizations; strong results on relationship detection (AUC 0.992), routing (0.672 vs 0.665 baseline), and phylogenetic analysis; extensive ablations on embedding models, DNA dimension, and pre-aggregation dimension
Extensive stress testing: Stability demonstrated across heterogeneous datasets (Mantel r=0.78), random inputs, chat template variations, and fine-tuning scenarios
Strong reproducibility: Full model list provided, detailed experimental setup, proofs in appendices, promised code release, PyPI package
Clear presentation and visualization: Well-motivated introduction, intuitive explanations, effective use of t-SNE visualization and phylogenetic trees
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: Theory assumes finite input length m and defines distance over full input space, but practice uses stochastic approximation on 600 arbitrary samples; Hilbert distance dH never directly computed; connection between bi-Lipschitz condition and semantic embeddings lacks rigorous justification

Understated semantic embedding dependency: Method fundamentally depends on choice of sentence-embedding model despite 'LLM-agnostic' claims; semantic embeddings compress outputs discarding information—not theoretically justified beyond intuition

Ground truth and evaluation concerns: Hugging Face Model Tree incomplete/incorrect, evidenced by higher recall (0.957) than precision (0.898), suggesting many 'false positives' are true relationships; 11 models in EmbedLLM routing comparison no longer exist; PhyloLM compared on non-native task (relationship detection vs. benchmark prediction)
Unclear scalability: 305 models require ~20TB storage and high-end GPUs; method scales to ~300 LLMs but unclear for millions; DNA dimension L=128 specific to this scale and may require retuning

No mathematical meaning to DNA subsequences: Section 5.7 observes fine-tuning alters specific subsequences suggesting trait encoding, but Definition 3.2 assigns no mathematical meaning to them (acknowledged in limitations); limits interpretability and utility

Bi-Lipschitz constants and hyperparameters not principled: Constants c₁, c₂ in Theorem 3.3 never estimated; sample size t=600 appears arbitrary without sensitivity analysis; concentration bound requirement Cmax never verified empirically
Adaptive attack vulnerability: DNA not robust to adaptive attacks if extraction procedure known; acknowledged but unresolved beyond keeping datasets closed-source
Modest performance improvements: Model routing improvement marginal (0.672 vs 0.665 EmbedLLM) with overlapping confidence intervals
Limited scope: Only text-generation models; no multimodal, encoder-only, or non-standard architectures; for encoder-decoder models, only decoder responses used
Statistical concerns: Some metric differences in Table 1 within standard deviations; lacks formal significance testing; probability measure μ in Lemma A.4 unspecified
